name: Next Generation Science Standards
subject: Science and engineering
owner: NGSS Lead States. "NGSS" is a registered trademark of WestEd.
adoption: Twenty states and the District of Columbia use the NGSS as written. About forty-four states use science standards built on the same National Research Council framework.
code_help: MS-PS3-3 reads as: middle school, Physical Science, core idea 3 (Energy), third performance expectation.

standards.summary: Investigate what makes an electric or magnetic force stronger or weaker.
Show that objects can push or pull each other without touching.
Describe how a moving object's energy depends on its mass and speed.
Model how stored energy changes when objects in a system move relative to each other.
Design and improve a device that moves heat energy where you want it.
Plan an experiment about what changes an object's temperature.
Argue from evidence that energy moves into or out of an object when it speeds up or slows down.
Use a mathematical model to describe how waves carry energy.
Explain why digital signals are a more reliable way to send information than analogue ones.
State clearly what a design has to achieve and what limits it, before starting to build.
Compare competing designs against the same set of criteria, methodically.
Test several designs, then combine the best parts of each into a better one.
Build, test, change, and test again until the design works well.
Calculate how energy moves between parts of a system when one part changes.
Design and build a device that converts one form of energy into another.
Use a model to predict how objects interact through electric or magnetic fields.
Evaluate why digital transmission and storage dominate modern electronics.
Break a large design problem into smaller ones that can be solved separately.
Weigh a design against cost, safety, reliability, and its effect on people.
